comp_1.title: Comprehension Passage 1: Artificial Intelligence & The Future of African Youth
comp_1.text:
The rapid ascension of artificial intelligence (AI) has ignited fervent debates across global economic and educational spheres. For the African continent, a demographic titan where over sixty percent of the populace is under the age of twenty-five, AI presents a precarious dichotomy: an unprecedented catalyst for developmental leapfrogging or a catastrophic amplifier of existing socio-economic disparities.

Historically, Africa remained on the periphery of the first three industrial revolutions, largely serving as a reservoir of raw materials rather than an architect of technological epochs. The fourth industrial revolution, however, is fundamentally democratized by compute and code. Young software engineers from Lagos to Nairobi, armed with modest laptops and ubiquitous internet connectivity, are devising localized AI models to diagnose crop ailments in cassava, streamline cross-border fintech remittances, and optimize logistics in congested metropolitan hubs.

Nevertheless, palpable impediments threaten to abort this technological renaissance. Intermittent electrical power supply, exorbitant broadband tariffs, and archaic academic curricula perpetuate a severe digital chasm. Furthermore, the global trend towards automation poses a lethal threat to entry-level business process outsourcing (BPO) occupations—traditionally the entry ramp for educated youths into the formal economy. If African governments merely spectate while developed nations monopolize algorithmic patents and computational infrastructure, the continent risks exchanging historic colonial subjugation for algorithmic neo-imperialism.

To circumvent this dystopian trajectory, a seismic paradigm shift is imperative. Educational institutions must aggressively recalibrate their pedagogical frameworks from rote memorization toward computational thinking, ethics, and applied machine learning. Concurrently, regional policymakers must establish sovereign data reserves and incentivize indigenous deep-tech venture ecosystems. The future will not be inherited by those who passively consume technological artefacts, but by those who audaciously build them.

comp_2.title: Comprehension Passage 2: Environmental Degradation & Climate Resilience in the Sahel
comp_2.text:
The Sahelian belt of West Africa occupies a tenuous ecological equilibrium. Flanked to the north by the hyper-arid expanse of the Sahara and to the south by the humid Guinea savannah, this semi-arid corridor has for centuries sustained pastoralist and agrarian communities through intricately negotiated migratory patterns and regenerative fallow cycles.

In recent decades, however, this fragile truce between man and nature has ruptured. Accelerating climatological shifts, characterized by erratic precipitation patterns and protracted droughts, have exacerbated land degradation. Topsoils, stripped of vegetative cover through unsustainable deforestation and overgrazing, succumb to aeolian erosion. The Sahara relentlessly advances southward at an estimated rate of several kilometres annually—a phenomenon colloquially known as desertification.

The ramifications transcend mere environmental distress; they constitute the bedrock of acute geopolitical volatility. Shrinking arable lands and diminished water reservoirs, most notably epitomized by the precipitous shrinking of Lake Chad to a fraction of its mid-twentieth-century volume, have triggered fierce clashes between sedentary farmers and nomadic Fulani herders. Deprived of customary livelihoods, disaffected youths become vulnerable to conscription by trans-border insurgent factions operating across ungoverned territories.

Technical remediations exist, most visibly embodied in the ambitious 'Great Green Wall' initiative—a transcontinental pan-African rampart of trees spanning from Senegal in the west to Djibouti in the east. Yet, agronomic scientists caution that mere afforestation is inadequate without accompanying socio-economic reforms. Holistic soil restoration, tenure security for vulnerable peasants, and the deployment of drought-resilient cultivars must supersede superficial tree-planting ceremonies if lasting ecological equilibrium is to be restored.

However, recognizing the immense potential of digital payment gateways to accelerate financial (5)___ among previously unbanked rural populations, central banks eventually adopted more accommodating regulatory sandboxes.

Nonetheless, this hyper-connected financial landscape is not without serious (6)___. Cybercriminals continually devise sophisticated social engineering schemes, phishing portals, and identity theft mechanisms to (7)___ unsuspecting depositors of their hard-earned assets. Consequently, commercial banks must invest (8)___ in robust cybersecurity firewalls and multi-factor biometric authentication infrastructure. Ultimately, safeguarding trust remains the paramount (10)___ upon which the longevity of digital finance depends.

cloze_2.title: Cloze Passage 2: The Art of Medical Diagnosis
cloze_2.text:
Clinical medicine is both a rigorous science and a nuanced art. When a patient presents at a clinic with ambiguous symptoms, the examining physician must avoid premature (11)___ and instead conduct a systematic investigation. The first step involves eliciting a comprehensive medical (12)___, which provides essential contextual clues regarding the onset, duration, and trajectory of the ailment.

Next, a meticulous physical examination is performed to identify objective clinical (13)___, such as abnormal heart murmurs or abdominal tenderness, which substantiate or contradict the patient's subjective complaints. If the clinical picture remains (14)___, the doctor orders targeted haematological and radiological investigations. Indiscriminate prescription of medications prior to establishing an accurate diagnosis can be exceedingly (15)___ to patient well-being.

Once all diagnostic parameters have been synthesized, the physician formulates a working hypothesis, termed a (16)___ diagnosis. This guides the implementation of a tailored therapeutic regimen. In severe pathologies, timely clinical intervention can (17)___ irreversible organ failure and significantly lower patient (18)___. Patients are strongly urged to adhere strictly to the prescribed dosage schedule and not (19)___ treatment midway simply because acute discomfort has subsided. Vigilant post-treatment follow-up ensures that latent relapses are promptly (20)___.

P1.title: Passage P1
P1.text: In many Nigerian cities, the movement of young people from rural villages in search of work has reshaped both the towns they leave and the cities they enter. Villages once busy with farming now rely on a shrinking number of older residents to keep tradition alive, while urban centres strain under the weight of new arrivals seeking jobs that often do not exist. Some analysts argue that this movement, if properly managed through rural investment and skills training, could still benefit the nation as a whole. Others warn that without deliberate policy, the imbalance will only deepen, leaving villages hollowed out and cities overcrowded.

P2.title: Passage P2
P2.text: Access to reliable electricity remains one of the most persistent challenges facing small businesses across Nigeria. A tailor who cannot power a sewing machine, or a barber who cannot run clippers, often loses income during outages that can stretch for hours or even days. In response, many entrepreneurs have turned to solar panels and battery inverters, accepting the upfront cost as an investment in stability. While these solutions have reduced dependence on the national grid for some, the initial expense remains out of reach for many of the smallest businesses, meaning the benefits of self-generated power are not yet shared equally.

comp_3.title: Comprehension Passage 3: Genetic Engineering & Bioethics
comp_3.text:
The dawn of CRISPR-Cas9 genome editing technology has ushered humanity into an era of unprecedented genetic manipulation. Unlike earlier transgenic techniques that were cumbersome and imprecise, CRISPR functions with molecular scalpel precision, allowing researchers to excise, modify, or insert targeted genetic sequences with relative ease.

In clinical therapeutics, the prospects are undeniably exhilarating. Severe monogenic disorders such as sickle cell anaemia, a hereditary haemoglobinopathy endemic in sub-Saharan Africa, have shown dramatic curative responses in early clinical trials. By extracting haematopoietic stem cells from patients, editing the mutated beta-globin gene, and re-infusing the corrected cells, researchers have effectively alleviated debilitating vaso-occlusive crises in afflicted individuals.

However, the bioethical ramifications of germline genetic modification provoke deep philosophical alarm. Unlike somatic cell therapy—where modifications remain confined to the treated individual—germline edits alter the DNA of reproductive gametes or early embryos, ensuring that changes are permanently transmitted to all succeeding generations. Ethicists warn that if commercialized without stringent international oversight, this technology could spawn a dystopia of 'designer babies,' widening societal stratifications between a genetically enhanced elite and a biologically unaugmented underclass.

The consensus among global bioethics councils is that while somatic gene editing for fatal pathologies should be rigorously accelerated, germline alterations for aesthetic or non-medical enhancements must be strictly interdicted. Humankind must exercise profound humility, recognizing that manipulating the fundamental genetic code of our species carries irrevocable ecological and evolutionary consequences.

questions.question: Salma's initial arrogant perception of tertiary institutions as spaces of unbridled liberty was radically shattered when:

questions.option_c: She was denied entry into the campus hostel by the porter

questions.question: Which character serves as a foil to Salma's flamboyant and deceitful lifestyle at the university?

questions.question: What does the term 'Life Changer' metaphorically symbolize in the context of the novel?

questions.option_b: The transformative transition into university life, which fundamentally tests character and moral choices
questions.option_c: The migration from northern Nigeria to Lagos
questions.option_d: The procurement of a smartphone by secondary school graduates

questions.question: How did Salma manage to overcome her legal and emotional distress after her expulsion from the university?

questions.question: What central moral lesson does Ummi seek to impart to Omar as he prepares for matriculation?
questions.option_a: That academic success is purely a product of luck rather than discipline
questions.option_b: That university freedom requires vigilant self-restraint and unwavering moral integrity

questions.option_d: That family loyalty should be abandoned once one achieves financial independence

questions.question: Choose the option that is most nearly OPPOSITE in meaning to the word in CAPITAL letters: The minister made an ARBITRARY decision without consulting the board.
questions.explanation: Arbitrary means based on random choice or personal whim rather than reason or system. Its antonym is 'methodical' (systematic, well-ordered).

questions.question: Choose the option most nearly OPPOSITE in meaning to the CAPITALIZED word: The defendant was completely EXONERATED by the appellate court.
questions.explanation: Exonerated means declared free from guilt or blame. The direct opposite is 'convicted' (found guilty of a criminal offence).

questions.question: Choose the option most nearly OPPOSITE in meaning to the CAPITALIZED word: His speech was surprisingly LUCID despite the technical complexity of the topic.
questions.explanation: Lucid means clear, easily understood, and intelligible. Its antonym is 'obscure' (unclear, ambiguous, difficult to comprehend).

questions.question: Choose the option most nearly OPPOSITE in meaning to the CAPITALIZED word: The newly appointed chairman was commended for his FRUGAL management of company resources.
questions.explanation: Frugal means sparing or economical with regard to money. The opposite is 'extravagant' (wastefully spending money or resources).

questions.question: Choose the option most nearly OPPOSITE in meaning to the CAPITALIZED word: The athlete displayed a PUSILLANIMOUS attitude in the face of defeat.
questions.explanation: Pusillanimous means lacking courage or resolution; cowardly. Its exact opposite is 'courageous' (brave, valiant).

questions.question: Choose the option NEAREST IN MEANING to the word in CAPITAL letters: The old professor was known for his ERUDITE commentaries on constitutional law.
questions.explanation: Erudite means having or showing profound knowledge; scholarly and well-learned.

questions.question: Choose the option NEAREST IN MEANING to the CAPITALIZED word: The CEO was accused of practicing NEPOTISM in executive appointments.
questions.explanation: Nepotism refers to the practice among those with power or influence of favouring relatives or friends, especially by giving them jobs.

questions.question: Choose the option NEAREST IN MEANING to the CAPITALIZED word: The diplomat handled the delicate dispute with commendable TACT.
questions.explanation: Tact is skill and sensitivity in dealing with others or with difficult issues; diplomacy and discretion.

questions.question: Choose the option NEAREST IN MEANING to the CAPITALIZED word: The community leader gave a TERSENESS to his final verdict that left no room for doubt.
questions.explanation: Terse means brief and to the point; conciseness or succinctness without superfluous words.

questions.question: Choose the option NEAREST IN MEANING to the CAPITALIZED word: The evidence presented by the prosecution was entirely SPURIOUS.
questions.explanation: Spurious means not being what it purports to be; false, counterfeit, or fabricated.

questions.question: Interpret the statement: 'The auditor was caught between the devil and the deep blue sea.' This means the auditor:
questions.option_a: Was on a maritime voyage during a severe hurricane
questions.option_b: Faced two equally dangerous or unpleasant alternatives
questions.option_c: Decided to compromise with the corrupt officials
questions.option_d: Escaped unscathed from a dangerous confrontation
questions.explanation: The idiom 'between the devil and the deep blue sea' signifies being in a dilemma where one must choose between two undesirable courses of action.

questions.question: Interpret: 'When the crisis erupted, the commissioner passed the buck.' This means the commissioner:
questions.option_a: Donated large sums of money to the emergency relief fund
questions.option_b: Shifted the responsibility and blame onto someone else
questions.explanation: 'Pass the buck' is an established idiom meaning to shift responsibility or blame to another person.

questions.question: Interpret: 'His explanation of the financial discrepancies was a cock-and-bull story.' This means his explanation was:
questions.option_a: Derived from a popular folklore concerning farm animals
questions.option_b: Incredible and fabricated to deceive his listeners
questions.option_c: Validated by reputable independent forensic accountants
questions.option_d: Delivered with great anger and hostility
questions.explanation: A 'cock-and-bull story' is an absurd, implausible, and fabricated tale used as an excuse.

questions.question: Interpret: 'The project manager threw in the towel after funding was rescinded.' This means the project manager:
questions.option_a: Washed all dirty linen in the laundry room
questions.option_b: Admitted defeat and surrendered the endeavor
questions.option_c: Appealed directly to the board of trustees for additional grants
questions.option_d: Celebrated the successful completion of the assignment
questions.explanation: To 'throw in the towel' is an idiom derived from boxing meaning to surrender, admit defeat, or abandon a struggle.

questions.question: Interpret: 'The candidate took the news of his score with a grain of salt.' This means the candidate:
questions.option_a: Added salt to his meal while listening to the radio
questions.option_b: Received the news with scepticism and did not accept it completely
questions.option_c: Broke down into uncontrollable tears of sorrow
questions.option_d: Immediately forwarded the news to all his family members
questions.explanation: To take something 'with a grain of salt' means to view it with scepticism and reserve judgment regarding its absolute truth.

questions.question: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: The committee _____ decided to submit its final report next month.
questions.explanation: When a collective noun like 'committee' acts as a unified singular body, it takes a singular verb ('has').

questions.question: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: Neither the governor nor his commissioners _____ present at the groundbreaking ceremony.
questions.explanation: According to the rule of proximity in concord, when correlative conjunctions 'neither...nor' join subjects of different numbers, the verb agrees with the nearer subject ('commissioners' -> plural -> 'were').

questions.question: Choose the correct option: I demand that he _____ immediately to the disciplinary committee.
questions.explanation: The present subjunctive mood is used after verbs of demand, request, or recommendation ('demand that he apologize' - base form of the verb).

questions.question: Choose the correct option: The juvenile delinquent was charged _____ armed robbery and unlawful possession of firearms.
questions.explanation: The standard legal idiom in English is to be 'charged with' a crime (compare: 'accused of' a crime).

questions.question: Choose the correct option: Had I known you were stranded at the terminus, I _____ to pick you up.
questions.explanation: This is a third conditional inversion expressing past unfulfilled hypothesis: 'Had I known... I would have come'.

questions.question: From the options lettered A to D, choose the word that contains the SAME VOWEL SOUND as the one represented by the underlined letter(s): b<l><u><o>d
questions.explanation: The vowel sound in 'blood' is the short central open vowel /ʌ/ (as in cup, flood, sun). 'Food' and 'fool' have /uː/, and 'book' has /ʊ/.

questions.question: Choose the word that contains the SAME DIPHTHONG sound as the underlined letter(s): c<o><a coat
questions.explanation: 'Coat' has the diphthong /əʊ/ (as in 'boat', 'go', 'home'). 'Court' and 'caught' have the monophthong /ɔː/, while 'cost' has /ɒ/.

questions.question: From the options lettered A to D, choose the word that contains the SAME CONSONANT SOUND as the one represented by the underlined letters: <ph>one
questions.explanation: The letters 'ph' in 'phone' represent the voiceless labiodental fricative /f/, exactly as in 'physics'. In 'psychology' and 'pneumonia', the letter 'p' is silent.

questions.question: In which of the following words is the letter 'b' SILENT?
questions.explanation: In 'subtle' (pronounced /ˈsʌt.əl/), the letter 'b' is silent. In 'table', 'blanket', and 'timber', 'b' is voiced.

questions.question: From the options lettered A to D, choose the word that RHYMES with: suite
questions.explanation: 'Suite' is pronounced exactly as /swiːt/, rhyming perfectly with 'sweet'. 'Suit' is pronounced /suːt/ or /sjuːt/.

questions.question: From the options lettered A to D, choose the word that RHYMES with: reign
questions.explanation: 'Reign' is pronounced /reɪn/, forming an exact homophone and rhyme with 'rain'.

questions.question: Choose the option with the correct PRIMARY STRESS pattern for the word: PHOTOGRAPH
questions.explanation: The noun 'photograph' is stressed on the first syllable: /ˈfəʊ.tə.ɡrɑːf/ (PHO-to-graph). Compare with pho-TO-gra-pher and pho-to-GRA-phic.

questions.question: Choose the option with the correct PRIMARY STRESS pattern for the word: DEMOCRACY
questions.explanation: Words ending in the suffix '-cracy' carry primary stress on the antepenultimate syllable (third from end): de-MO-cra-cy /dɪˈmɒk.rə.si/.

questions.question: In the sentence below, the word in CAPITAL letters has the emphatic stress: 'Ngozi bought a BRAND-NEW bicycle for her brother.' To which of the following questions is this sentence the appropriate answer?
questions.option_a: Did Ngozi buy a second-hand bicycle for her brother?
questions.option_b: Did Ngozi sell a brand-new bicycle for her brother?
questions.option_c: Did Ngozi buy a brand-new motorcycle for her brother?
questions.option_d: Did Emeka buy a brand-new bicycle for her brother?
questions.explanation: Emphatic stress highlights the contrast. Stressing 'BRAND-NEW' directly contradicts and answers 'Did Ngozi buy a second-hand bicycle...?'

questions.question: In the sentence below, the word in CAPITAL letters has the emphatic stress: 'The GOVERNOR donated five ambulances to the hospital yesterday.' Which question does this sentence answer?
questions.option_a: Did the senator donate five ambulances to the hospital yesterday?
questions.option_b: Did the governor sell five ambulances to the hospital yesterday?
questions.option_c: Did the governor donate ten ambulances to the hospital yesterday?
questions.option_d: Did the governor donate five ambulances to the school yesterday?
questions.explanation: Stressing 'GOVERNOR' emphasizes WHO made the donation, directly correcting the question 'Did the senator donate...?'

questions.option_a: Villages and cities will both flourish equally
questions.option_b: The imbalance between rural and urban areas will deepen
questions.option_d: Jobs will immediately increase in cities

questions.question: Which word from the passage is closest in meaning to 'persistent'?
questions.explanation: 'Persistent' means continuing to exist over a long period, matching 'continuing without stopping'

questions.question: Choose the word that best completes gap (1) in the passage.

questions.question: Choose the word that best completes gap (2) in the passage.

questions.question: Choose the word that best completes gap (4) in the passage.

questions.question: Choose the word that best completes gap (5) in the passage.

questions.question: Choose the word that best completes gap (6) in the passage.

questions.question: Choose the word that is nearest in meaning to the underlined word: The politician's speech was full of RHETORIC.
questions.explanation: Rhetoric refers to language designed to persuade, often at the expense of sincerity

questions.question: Choose the word nearest in meaning to: The old bridge was considered DILAPIDATED.
questions.explanation: Dilapidated means falling into disrepair or ruin

questions.question: Choose the word nearest in meaning to: Her explanation was remarkably LUCID.
questions.explanation: Lucid means expressed clearly and is easy to understand

questions.question: Choose the word nearest in meaning to: The manager's decision was completely ARBITRARY.

questions.question: Choose the word nearest in meaning to: The witness gave a CANDID account of events.

questions.question: Choose the word most nearly OPPOSITE in meaning to: The politician's remarks were considered CANDID.

questions.question: Choose the word most nearly OPPOSITE in meaning to: The evidence presented was CONCLUSIVE.

questions.question: Choose the word most nearly OPPOSITE in meaning to: The old man was known for his GENEROSITY.
questions.explanation: Generosity means being willing to give freely, so its opposite is stinginess

questions.question: Choose the word most nearly OPPOSITE in meaning to: The instructions were surprisingly AMBIGUOUS.
questions.explanation: Ambiguous means open to more than one interpretation, so its opposite is clear

questions.question: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: Neither the teacher nor the students ___ aware of the change in schedule.
questions.explanation: When 'neither...nor' joins a singular and plural subject, the verb agrees with the nearer subject, here 'students', requiring 'were'

questions.question: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: By the time the announcement was made, the students ___ already left the hall.
questions.explanation: The past perfect tense 'had already left' is required to show an action completed before another past action

questions.question: Choose the correct preposition to complete the sentence: The company is known ___ its excellent customer service.
questions.explanation: The correct idiomatic preposition after 'known' when referring to reputation is 'for'

questions.question: Choose the correct preposition to complete the sentence: She was accused ___ stealing from the company.
questions.explanation: The correct preposition following 'accused' is 'of', as in 'accused of a crime'

questions.question: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: If I ___ known about the meeting, I would have attended.
questions.explanation: The third conditional requires the past perfect 'had known' paired with 'would have attended'

questions.question: Which of the following sentences is grammatically correct?

questions.option_b: Each of the students has submitted their assignment
questions.option_c: Each of the student have submit their assignment
questions.option_d: Each of the students submitting their assignment

questions.question: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: The report, along with the supporting documents, ___ due tomorrow.
questions.explanation: When a phrase like 'along with' follows the subject, the verb still agrees with the singular subject 'report', requiring 'is'

questions.question: Choose the correctly punctuated sentence.
questions.explanation: The contraction 'it's' meaning 'it is' requires an apostrophe, making this option correctly punctuated

questions.question: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: The two brothers have been quarreling ___ themselves since childhood.
questions.explanation: 'Among themselves' is the idiomatic expression used when referring to more than two people or a mutual group, though here 'among' is accepted idiomatically with 'brothers' as a set

questions.question: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: Hardly ___ the meeting begun when the fire alarm went off.
questions.explanation: 'Hardly had...when' is a fixed inverted structure using the past perfect tense to describe two closely sequenced past events

questions.question: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: The committee _____ to submit its report by Friday.

questions.question: The word 'interdicted' as used in the final paragraph most nearly means:

questions.question: Choose the word OPPOSITE in meaning to the capitalized word: The doctor described the patient's condition as PRECARIOUS.
questions.explanation: Precarious means dangerously insecure or unstable. Its opposite is 'stable'.

questions.question: Choose the word OPPOSITE in meaning: The judge noted that the witness was remarkably COGNIZANT of the facts.
questions.explanation: Cognizant means having knowledge or awareness. Its antonym is 'ignorant'.

questions.question: Choose the word OPPOSITE in meaning: Her brother is notoriously PENURIOUS.
questions.explanation: Penurious means destitute or extremely stingy. Its opposite is 'affluent' (wealthy, generous).

questions.question: Choose the word OPPOSITE in meaning: The treaty was intended to CONCILIATE the rebellious tribes.
questions.explanation: Conciliate means to stop from being angry; placate. Opposite is 'alienate' (estrange, provoke).

questions.question: Choose the word OPPOSITE in meaning: The evidence against the accused was COGENT.
questions.explanation: Cogent means clear, logical, and convincing. Opposite is 'unconvincing'.

questions.question: Choose the word OPPOSITE in meaning: The general launched an AUDACIOUS counter-attack.
questions.explanation: Audacious means showing a willingness to take surprisingly bold risks. Opposite is 'timid'.

questions.question: Choose the word OPPOSITE in meaning: The climate in the plateau region is TEMPERATE.
questions.explanation: Temperate means moderate in climate. Opposite is 'extreme'.

questions.question: Choose the word OPPOSITE in meaning: His remarks were deemed INNOCUOUS.
questions.explanation: Innocuous means not harmful or offensive. Opposite is 'harmful'.

questions.question: Choose the word NEAREST in meaning: The professor's lecture was completely INCOMPREHENSIBLE to the freshmen.
questions.explanation: Incomprehensible means impossible to understand; unintelligible.

questions.question: Choose the word NEAREST in meaning: The accountant was commended for his METICULOUS record keeping.
questions.explanation: Meticulous means showing great attention to detail; very careful and painstaking.

questions.question: Choose the word NEAREST in meaning: The senator's popularity began to WANE after the scandal.
questions.explanation: To wane means to decrease in vigour, power, or extent; diminish.

questions.question: Choose the word NEAREST in meaning: The university senate decided to RESCIND the controversial regulation.
questions.explanation: Rescind means to revoke, cancel, or repeal a law or agreement.

questions.question: Choose the word NEAREST in meaning: The old man lived an AUSTERE life in the mountains.
questions.explanation: Austere means severe or strict in manner, living very simply without luxuries (ascetic).

questions.question: Choose the word NEAREST in meaning: The minister's speech was full of PLATITUDES.
questions.explanation: A platitude is a remark or statement, especially one with a moral content, that has been used too often to be interesting or thoughtful.

questions.question: Choose the word NEAREST in meaning: The new recruit was unusually RETICENT about his past.
questions.explanation: Reticent means not revealing one's thoughts or feelings readily; reserved.

questions.question: Choose the word NEAREST in meaning: The athlete showed RESILIENCE after his injury.
questions.explanation: Resilience is the capacity to recover quickly from difficulties; toughness.

questions.question: Choose the correct option: The news broadcast on the radio _____ alarming.
questions.explanation: 'News' is an uncountable noun that takes a singular verb ('was').

questions.question: Choose the correct option: Each of the candidates _____ given a question booklet.
questions.explanation: 'Each' is an indefinite pronoun that takes a singular verb ('was').

questions.question: Choose the correct option: Ten thousand naira _____ too much to pay for that textbook.
questions.explanation: Expressions of amount, time, distance, or money take a singular verb when considered as a unit ('is').

questions.question: Choose the correct option: Neither the coach nor the players _____ happy with the officiating.
questions.explanation: Correlative conjunctions agree with the nearer subject ('players' -> plural -> 'were').

questions.question: Choose the correct option: If he _____ earlier, he would not have missed the bus.
questions.explanation: Third conditional: 'If + past perfect (had left) ... would have + past participle'.

questions.question: Choose the correct option: The boy preferred playing football _____ reading novels.
questions.explanation: The verb 'prefer' takes the preposition 'to', not 'than' (e.g., 'prefer X to Y').

questions.question: Choose the correct option: The principal congratulated the students _____ their outstanding performance.
questions.explanation: The standard preposition after 'congratulate' is 'on' (congratulate someone on something).

questions.question: Choose the correct option: She has been living in Abuja _____ 2015.
questions.explanation: 'Since' is used for a specific starting point in time, while 'for' is used for a duration.

questions.question: Choose the correct option: The criminal was accused _____ arson and grand theft.
questions.explanation: One is 'accused of' a crime, but 'charged with' a crime.

questions.question: Choose the correct option: He spoke as though he _____ the absolute owner of the estate.
questions.explanation: Hypothetical unreal comparison with 'as though' takes the past subjunctive 'were'.

questions.question: Choose the word containing the same vowel sound as: <k><i><d>
questions.explanation: The vowel in 'kid' is short /ɪ/, which is found in 'busy' /ˈbɪz.i/. 'Buy' and 'bite' have /aɪ/, and 'key' has /iː/.

questions.question: Choose the word containing the same vowel sound as: <f><a><t><h><e><r>
questions.explanation: 'Father' has the long back vowel /ɑː/, which is also heard in 'car' /kɑːr/.

questions.question: Choose the word containing the same vowel sound as: s<e><a><t>
questions.explanation: 'Seat' has the long close front vowel /iː/, identical to the vowel in 'key' /kiː/.

In which of the following words is the letter 'w' SILENT?
Choose the word containing the same consonant sound as: <c><h>urch
questions.explanation: 'Church' and 'charity' have the voiceless postalveolar affricate /tʃ/. 'Chemist' and 'chorus' have /k/, while 'chauffeur' has /ʃ/.

questions.question: Choose the word that RHYMES with: debt
questions.explanation: 'Debt' is pronounced /det/, which rhymes with 'met'. 'B' is silent.

questions.question: Choose the word that RHYMES with: tomb
questions.explanation: 'Tomb' is pronounced /tuːm/, rhyming with 'womb' /wuːm/. 'Comb' is /kəʊm/ and 'bomb' is /bɒm/.

questions.question: Choose the word stressed on the FIRST syllable:
questions.explanation: 'Telephone' is stressed on the 1st syllable: /ˈtel.ɪ.fəʊn/ (TE-le-phone). 'Examine' and 'decision' are stressed on the 2nd, 'succeed' on the 2nd.

questions.question: Choose the word stressed on the SECOND syllable:
questions.explanation: 'Economy' is stressed on the 2nd syllable: /ɪˈkɒn.ə.mi/ (e-CO-no-my). 'Government', 'politics', and 'physics' are stressed on the 1st.

questions.question: Choose the word stressed on the THIRD syllable:
questions.explanation: 'Democratic' /ˌdem.əˈkræt.ɪk/, 'education' /ˌedʒ.uˈkeɪ.ʃən/, and 'understand' /ˌʌn.dəˈstænd/ are all stressed on the third syllable.

questions.question: In: 'ADE borrowed my physics textbook yesterday.' (Emphatic stress on ADE). Which question does this answer?
questions.option_a: Did Ade steal your physics textbook yesterday?
questions.option_b: Did Ade borrow your chemistry textbook yesterday?
questions.option_c: Did Bola borrow your physics textbook yesterday?
questions.option_d: Did Ade borrow your physics textbook today?
questions.explanation: Stressing 'ADE' contrasts with who borrowed the textbook ('Did Bola borrow...? No, ADE did').
